properties.headline: Marine Weather Statement issued September 16 at 2:15AM EDT by NWS Melbourne FL
properties.description:
A Marine Weather Statement has been issued for the following areas...
Volusia-Brevard County Line to Sebastian Inlet 0-20 nm...

At 213 AM EDT, Doppler radar indicated gusty showers and possibly a
thunderstorm, capable of producing winds to around 30 knots. This
convection was located offshore Brevard county, in particular 10 nm
east of Indialantic, moving west at 20 knots. These showers will
produce brief downpours and gusty winds as they push onshore and
across the intracoastal waters. Occasional lightning strikes are also
possible.
properties.instruction:
Mariners can expect gusty winds to around 30 knots, locally higher
waves, and lightning strikes. Boaters should seek safe harbor
immediately until this storm passes.

properties.description:
* WHAT...Flooding caused by excessive rainfall is expected.

* WHERE...Northern Chariton County in north central Missouri...
Southeastern Grundy County in north central Missouri...
Linn County in north central Missouri...
Livingston County in north central Missouri...
Macon County in north central Missouri...
Southeastern Putnam County in north central Missouri...
Northern Randolph County in north central Missouri...
Sullivan County in north central Missouri...
Adair County in northeastern Missouri...
Southern Schuyler County in northeastern Missouri...

* WHEN...Until 915 AM CDT Wednesday.

* IMPACTS...Minor flooding in low-lying and poor drainage areas.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- At 115 AM CDT, Doppler radar indicated heavy rain due to
thunderstorms. Minor flooding is ongoing or expected to begin

deaths occur in vehicles.

dangers of flooding.

properties.description:
* WHAT...Dangerous rip currents.

* WHERE...The beaches of Volusia, Brevard, Indian River, Saint
Lucie, and Martin Counties.

* WHEN...Through late tonight.

* IMPACTS...Rip currents can sweep even the best swimmers away
from shore into deeper water.
properties.instruction:

from shore, which occur most often at low spots or breaks in the
sandbar and in the vicinity of structures such as jetties and
piers. Heed the advice of lifeguards, beach patrol flags and
signs.

current, relax and float. Don't swim against the current. If
able, swim in a direction following the shoreline. If unable to
escape, face the shore and call or wave for help.

west central Arizona, including the following areas, in east
central Arizona, Northern Gila County. In north central Arizona,

possible.

* WHERE...Portions of central and west central New Mexico, including
the following areas, in central New Mexico, South Central
Mountains. In west central New Mexico, West Central Highlands, West
Central Mountains and West Central Plateau.

* WHEN...From Wednesday afternoon through late Wednesday night.

* IMPACTS...Excessive runoff may result in flooding of rivers,
creeks, streams, and other low-lying and flood-prone locations.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- Deep monsoon moisture will continue to move into western and
central New Mexico, helping numerous showers and thunderstorms to
develop. Stronger storms will be capable of producing heavy
rainfall rates of 1 to 2 inches per hour with some areas
receiving multiple rounds of storms. This will be too fast and
heavy for the ground to adequately absorb, leading to excessive
runoff and flash flooding.

Recent wildfire burn scars within Lincoln county will be
especially vulnerable to flash flooding.

properties.headline: Flood Advisory issued September 15 at 9:32PM AKDT until September 16 at 7:00AM AKDT by NWS Anchorage AK
properties.description:
* WHAT...Flooding caused by onshore flow restricting Kuskokwim River
drainage in combination with excessive rainfall is expected.

* WHERE...Kuskokwim near Bethel.

* WHEN...Until 700 AM AKDT Wednesday.

* IMPACTS...Minor flooding in low-lying and poor drainage areas.
River or stream flows are elevated. Ponding of water in areas is
occurring or is imminent.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- At 900 PM AKDT, River gauge reports indicate that receding water
levels have begun to rise again near Bethel, which remains at
minor flood stage. This is due to the Kuskokwim River back-up in
combination with heavy rain across the advisory area. Minor
flooding will continue from overflow of poor drainage areas,
especially along the Kuskokwim.
- Strong onshore winds along the Kuskokwim coast have limited the
ability for the Kuskokwim River to drain out into the Bering Sea.
This has caused rapid river rises along the coast and inland into
Bethel. Water levels are expected to back up along Brown Slough
and flood low lying areas of Bethel and areas along the
Kuskokwim.
- For Kuskokwim River at Bethel:
At 8:51pm the stage was 9.1 feet.
Flood Stage is 8.5 feet.

Impacts:
At 7.0 feet: Action and bankfull stage.
At 8.5 feet: Minor flood stage. Water starts to back up along Brown
Slough and flood low lying areas.
At 12.0 feet: Moderate flood stage.
At 14.0 feet: Major flood stage.


- Http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood
properties.instruction:
Stay tuned to further developments by listening to your local radio,
television, or NOAA Weather Radio for further information.

Be especially cautious at night when it is harder to recognize the
dangers of flooding.

If you live near or along the Kuskokwim River stay alert and be
prepared to take action.

properties.description:
* WHAT...Flooding caused by excessive rainfall continues to be
possible.

* WHERE...The southern Gila Region in southwestern New Mexico,
including most of northern Grant County, and far western Sierra
County near the Black Range.

* WHEN...Through late Wednesday night.

* IMPACTS...Excessive runoff may result in flooding of rivers,
creeks, streams, and other low-lying and flood-prone locations.

crossings may be flooded.

disturbances will lead to rounds of thunderstorms capable of

may be slow to initiate in the higher terrain this afternoon, but
will become more numerous during the evening and late night
hours. Another round or two of storms is expected for Wednesday,
therefore the Flood Watch has been extended into early Thursday
morning.

properties.headline: Air Quality Alert issued September 15 at 5:02PM MST by NWS Phoenix AZ
properties.description:
* WHAT...The Imperial County APCD has issued an air quality alert
due to increased fine particle pollution from wildfire smoke.
Visit https://www.aqmd.gov/alertinfo to check current and forecasted
air quality levels.

* WHERE...Smoke from a fire in Mexico is moving towards western
Imperial County.. Levels of particle pollution can vary by time and
location depending on fire activity and local weather conditions.

* WHEN...tonight September 15 2026.

* IMPACTS...Particles in wildfire smoke can get deep into the lungs
and cause serious health problems such as heart attacks, strokes,
asthma attacks, and difficulty breathing. Everyone can be affected,
but people with lung or heart disease, older adults, people who are
pregnant, children, and those who spend a lot of time outdoors are
at greater risk.
properties.instruction:
To protect your health, if you smell or see smoke:

* Remain indoors with windows and doors closed
* Avoid intense outdoor physical activity
* Run your air conditioner and/or an air purifier
* If you must be outdoors, keep the time brief and wear a well-
fitting N-95 mask
* Do not use whole house fans or swamp coolers that bring in
outside air if you have other methods to stay cool
* Avoid other sources of pollution such as fireplaces, candles,
incense, grilling, and gasoline-powered lawn and garden
equipment
properties.note: Non-Weather Emergency Message. Not sent to IPAWS.

NWSheadline: AIR QUALITY ALERT FOR HARMFUL FINE PARTICLE POLLUTION LEVELS DUE TO WILDFIRE SMOKE

properties.areaDesc: SW Kenai Peninsula; NW Kenai Peninsula
properties.headline: Wind Advisory issued September 15 at 3:28PM AKDT until September 16 at 12:00PM AKDT by NWS Anchorage AK
properties.description:
* WHAT...South winds 15 to 25 mph with gusts of up to 40 to 50 mph
expected.

* WHERE...NW Kenai Peninsula and SW Kenai Peninsula.

* WHEN...Until noon AKDT Wednesday.

* IMPACTS...Gusty winds will blow around unsecured objects and a few
power outages may result. Trees are still mostly green and fully
leafed, causing them to be more vulnerable to damage from the
strong winds.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...A strong fall storm moving into the western
coast of Alaska will produce strong and gusty southerly winds
moving up the Cook Inlet starting this afternoon and persisting
into tomorrow morning. The strongest winds will be focused along
the coast from Anchor Point north to Kenai and Nikiski. The gusty
southerly winds will continue through late tomorrow morning before
slowly diminishing later in the afternoon.
properties.instruction:
Winds this strong can make driving difficult, especially for high
profile vehicles. Use extra caution.

Secure outdoor objects.

properties.areaDesc: Lower Matanuska Valley; Hatcher Pass; Southern Susitna Valley; Central Susitna Valley
properties.headline: Hydrologic Outlook issued September 15 at 3:20PM AKDT by NWS Anchorage AK
properties.description:
ESFAFC

Locations:

* Willow and Talkeetna
* Rivers, creeks, and streams with headwaters along the western
Talkeetna Mountains

Timing:

* Now through Wednesday (tomorrow) afternoon. Heaviest rainfall
expected from now through about midnight tonight.

Rainfall:

* The heaviest rain is ongoing. However, an estimated 1.5 to 2 inches
of rain have fallen along the Alaska Range and Talkeetna Mountains
so far today, with about 0.5 to 1 inches in Susitna Valley.
* Additional rainfall amounts of about 0.5 to 1.5 inches are forecast
from now through tomorrow afternoon.
* These rainfall totals likely won't be high enough for widespread
flooding, but smaller tributaries draining the Talkeetnas including
Willow Creek and the Little Susitna may reach bankfull.

Hydrologic Concerns:

* Many lower locations along rivers such as gravel bars and other
spots popular for camping and recreating may become inundated with
water with rivers reaching bankfull conditions.

* Heavy rain may result in localized ponding in low-lying areas and
locations with poor drainage.

Next Steps:

* Residents along area streams as well as river users and recreators
should anticipate higher than normal water levels and are advised
to monitor weather and river forecasts.

* Send weather or flooding reports to inws.ncep.noaa.gov/report/ or
by calling 1-907-266-5127.

* Reports on river conditions may be sent to the river forecast
center by calling 1-907-266-5160.

NWSheadline: SIGNIFICANT RAINFALL THROUGH TOMORROW AFTERNOON FOR THE MATANUSKA AND SUSITNA VALLEYS

properties.areaDesc: Kuskokwim Delta Coast and Nunivak Island
properties.headline: Coastal Flood Advisory issued September 15 at 3:12PM AKDT until September 16 at 10:00AM AKDT by NWS Anchorage AK
properties.description:
* WHAT...Water levels as high as 1.5 to 4.0 feet above the
normal highest tide line.

* WHERE...Kuskokwim Delta Coast, including Kwigillingok,
Kongiganak, Kipnuk, Toksook Bay, and Tununak.

* WHEN...From 1 PM Monday to 10 PM Tuesday.

* IMPACTS...Coastal flooding of low lying areas and erosion are
possible.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...A low pressure system in the eastern
Bering will continue to bring a strong fetch of
southwesterlies into the Kuskokwim Delta Coast today and
tonight. The highest water level increases will coincide with
high tides this morning and this afternoon. Conditions will
begin to improve overnight tonight into Wednesday morning as a
strong low pressure system exits the region.
properties.instruction:
A coastal flood advisory indicates that onshore winds and tides
will combine to generate flooding of low areas along the shore.

properties.areaDesc: Upper Kuskokwim Valley
properties.headline: Flood Watch issued September 15 at 2:21PM AKDT until September 18 at 4:00PM AKDT by NWS Fairbanks AK
properties.description:
* WHAT...Flooding caused by excessive rainfall is possible.

* WHERE...Including the following areas, Upper Kuskokwim Valley. This
includes the cities of McGrath, Nikolai, And Takotna.

* WHEN...Through Friday afternoon.

* IMPACTS...The Kuskokwim River is currently at bankfull. Soils
remain moist and excessive runoff may result in localized flooding
of rivers, creeks, streams, other low-lying areas and flood-prone
locations.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- Rain should continue through Wednesday afternoon with storm total
rainfall expected to be around 1 to 2 inches. Minor
pooling/ponding of water in low-lying and flood prone areas is
possible with the already saturated ground conditions beginning
on Tuesday. Small stream and creek flooding is possible as we
expect very high water levels throughout the week in response to
the heavy rain.

- We will continue to monitor the situation closely and update as
necessary.

- For more updated river information, please refer to
water.noaa.gov or weather.gov/aprfc
properties.instruction:
Stay tuned to further developments by listening to your local radio,
television, or NOAA Weather Radio for information.

Persons living along streams should stay alert and be prepared to
take action if a warning or advisory is issued, or flooding is
observed.

Those living in areas prone to flooding should be prepared to take
action should flooding develop.

Soils remain moist and excessive runoff may result in flooding of
rivers, creeks, streams, other low-lying areas and flood-prone
locations.

NWSheadline: FLOOD WATCH REMAINS IN EFFECT THROUGH FRIDAY AFTERNOON

properties.areaDesc: Two Rivers; Fairbanks Metro Area
properties.headline: Flood Watch issued September 15 at 2:21PM AKDT until September 19 at 4:00PM AKDT by NWS Fairbanks AK
properties.description:
* WHAT...Flooding caused by excessive rainfall is possible.

* WHERE...Including the following areas, Fairbanks, North Pole, Two
Rivers, Fort Wainwright, Ester, and Fox

* WHEN...Through Saturday afternoon.

* IMPACTS...Heavy rain may result in minor flooding of rivers,
creeks, streams, and other low-lying and flood-prone locations.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- The Chena River is running higher than normal and will continue
to be high through the week. Showers will continue through the
end of the week, with the bulk of the rainfall expected through
Thursday morning. Storm total rainfall during this time will be
around 0.50" to 1.00". It has been very wet lately and this
amount of rain has the potential to bring the Chena and Little
Chena Rivers above minor flood stage beginning Wednesday.

- This means low-lying and typical flood-prone areas may
experience areas of flooding from Wednesday through the end of
the week as water levels gradually rise then fall. In addition,
while we are not expecting much flooding away from rivers,
streams and creeks, as the ground is already saturated and may
struggle to hold more water. This can lead to pooling and ponding
of water across the area which may make travel difficult in
localized spots.

- There is some uncertainty with exact timing and amounts of
rainfall but as details become clearer, we will continue to
update.

- For more updated river information, please refer to
water.noaa.gov or weather.gov/aprfc
properties.instruction:
Stay tuned to further developments by listening to your local radio,
television, or NOAA Weather Radio for further information.

You should monitor the latest forecasts and be alert for possible
Flood Warnings. Those living in areas prone to flooding should be
prepared to take action should flooding develop.

properties.headline: Hydrologic Outlook issued September 15 at 2:15PM AKDT by NWS Fairbanks AK
properties.description:
ESFAFG

...Locations Impacted...
Middle Yukon Valley, Lower Koyukuk Valley, Lower Yukon Valley, and
Innoko Valley.

Across western Alaska, widespread 24 hour rainfall totals of between
0.75 1.00 inches were reported through Noon Tuesday. Additional
totals of 0.25 to 0.75" are possible with some locations potentially
seeing an additional 1.25 inches of additional rainfall through
Wednesday. While the Yukon river should be able to manage much of the
additional water, smaller streams and rivers that feed these systems
could experience some minor flooding over the next few days.

properties.headline: Flood Warning issued September 15 at 4:11PM CDT until September 17 at 4:00AM CDT by NWS Omaha/Valley NE
properties.description:
...The National Weather Service in Omaha/Valley has issued a Flood
Warning for the following rivers in Iowa...

East Nishnabotna River At Red Oak affecting Montgomery County.

* WHAT...Minor flooding is forecast.

* WHERE...East Nishnabotna River at Red Oak.

* WHEN...Until late Wednesday night.

* IMPACTS...At 20.0 feet, Lowland flooding begins along the west
bank.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- At 4:00 PM CDT Tuesday the stage was 17.6 feet.
- Bankfull stage is 18.0 feet.
- Forecast...The river is expected to rise above flood stage late
this afternoon to a crest of 19.7 feet just after midnight
tonight. It will then fall below flood stage by late tomorrow
morning.
- Flood stage is 18.0 feet.
- Flood History...This crest compares to a previous crest of 19.6
feet on 06/15/1980.
- http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood
properties.instruction:
Turn around, don't drown when encountering flooded roads. Most flood
deaths occur in vehicles.

Motorists should not attempt to drive around barricades or drive cars
through flooded areas.

Additional information is available at water.noaa.gov.

The next statement will be issued Wednesday afternoon at 100 PM CDT.

properties.areaDesc: San Rafael Swell; Capitol Reef National Park and Vicinity
properties.headline: Flood Watch issued September 15 at 11:58AM MDT until September 17 at 6:00AM MDT by NWS Salt Lake City UT
properties.description:
* WHAT...Flash flooding caused by excessive rainfall is possible.

* WHERE...A portion of Utah, including the following areas, San
Rafael Swell and Capitol Reef National Park and Vicinity.

* WHEN...From Wednesday afternoon through late Wednesday night.

* IMPACTS...Excessive runoff may result in flooding of rivers,
creeks, streams, dry washes, slot canyons, and other low-lying and
flood-prone locations such as slickrock areas and recent burn
scars.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- Deep moisture will remain in place across the region. Several
disturbances will fuel development of thunderstorms with rainfall
rates in excess of 0.25 to 0.50 inches per hour.  In areas with
training thunderstorms, rainfall rates will exceed 0.50 inches
per hour. This will cause flash flooding in areas such as
normally dry washes, slot canyons, and slickrock areas.
- http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood
properties.instruction:
You should monitor later forecasts and be prepared to take action
should Flash Flood Warnings be issued.

properties.areaDesc: Cooke
properties.headline: Heat Advisory issued September 15 at 12:32PM CDT until September 16 at 8:00PM CDT by NWS Fort Worth TX
properties.description:
* WHAT...Heat index values up to 105.

* WHERE...Cooke County.

* WHEN...Until 8 PM CDT Wednesday.

* IMPACTS...Hot temperatures and high humidity will increase the risk
for heat-related illnesses to occur, particularly for those working
or participating in outdoor activities.
properties.instruction:
Take extra precautions when outside by staying hydrated, wearing
lightweight and loose fitting clothing, and limiting strenuous
activities to the early morning or evening. Check up on relatives and
neighbors. Never leave young children or pets in an enclosed vehicle,
even for a short time, as temperatures can quickly rise to
life-threatening levels.

Know the signs and symptoms of heat exhaustion and heat stroke. To
reduce risk when outdoors, the occupational safety and health
administration recommends scheduling frequent rest breaks in shaded
or air conditioned environments. Anyone overcome by heat should be
moved to a cool and shaded location. Heat stroke is an emergency!
Call 911 ASAP if you or someone you know is exhibiting signs of heat
stroke.

properties.headline: Heat Advisory issued September 15 at 11:53AM CDT until September 18 at 8:00PM CDT by NWS St Louis MO
properties.description:
* WHAT...Heat index values up to 106.

* WHERE...Portions of south central and southwest Illinois and
central, east central, and southeast Missouri.

* WHEN...Until 8 PM CDT Friday.

* IMPACTS...Hot temperatures and high humidity may cause heat
illnesses.
properties.instruction:
Drink plenty of fluids, stay in an air-conditioned room, stay out of
the sun, and check up on relatives and neighbors. Young children and
pets should never be left unattended in vehicles under any
circumstances. Take extra precautions if you work or spend time
outside. When possible reschedule strenuous activities to early
morning or evening. Know the signs and symptoms of heat exhaustion
and heat stroke. Wear lightweight and loose fitting clothing when
possible. To reduce risk during outdoor work, the Occupational Safety
and Health Administration recommends scheduling frequent rest breaks
in shaded or air conditioned environments. Anyone overcome by heat
should be moved to a cool and shaded location. Heat stroke is an
emergency! Call 9 1 1.

People in the Saint Louis Metropolitan Area can get information about
cooling centers or energy assistance related to the excessive heat by
calling the United Way of Greater Saint Louis at 800-427-4626, or if
calling from a land line phone dial 2-1-1. You can also call Cool
Down Saint Louis at 314-241-7668.
